long_biography.plain_text:
Gabe Newell left Harvard for Microsoft, where he spent 13 years working across systems, applications and advanced technology and helped manage the first two Windows releases. In 1996 he cofounded Valve with former Microsoft colleague Mike Harrington. Half-Life, the company’s first game, became an immediate bestseller; Valve then used Half-Life 2 to accelerate Steam, turning a game studio into a major PC distribution platform while remaining privately held.

Valve is still the source of Newell’s fortune, and Forbes estimates that he owns at least half of the company. His later work has moved into ocean research through Inkfish. In 2026 the organisation contracted VARD to build RV11000, a 162-metre vessel designed for seafloor mapping, submarine support and remotely operated work down to 11,000 metres, with research data intended for open repositories. That programme gives his extensive maritime interests a documented scientific purpose rather than merely a collecting story.
